initialize.instructions:
This MCP server exposes the Acme Orders API (mock, writes enabled) through Neurouter.
Start every user request with neurouter_begin_task(goal) and finish with neurouter_end_task(outcome). If the user needs something no tool can do, call neurouter_report_unmet_need instead of guessing.
For multi-step work, prefer run_script: a short Python script (no imports, no I/O) that calls tools as acme.<fn>(...) and returns a small result. Get signatures with search_tools. Use mode="dry_run" first for anything that writes.
Errors include an error_id; neurouter_explain_error(error_id) tells you how to fix the call. Search "neurouter" to find the other helper tools.

tools_list.name: run_script
tools_list.title: Run a Python script against the API
tools_list.description: Run a short Python script that calls API tools as functions (e.g. acme.list_orders()) and returns a JSON-serializable value with `return`. No imports, no files, no network: only the tool functions, built-ins (len, sorted, isinstance, type, iter/next, …; no map/filter/getattr) and ops.* helpers. Tool results are whole dicts/lists inside scripts (no maxItems/maxBytes cuts); the script result limit applies to what you return. Use mode="dry_run" to see planned writes without executing them. Get function signatures from search_tools.

ro_initialize.instructions:
This MCP server exposes the Acme Orders API (ro, read-only) through Neurouter.
Start every user request with neurouter_begin_task(goal) and finish with neurouter_end_task(outcome). If the user needs something no tool can do, call neurouter_report_unmet_need instead of guessing.
For multi-step work, prefer run_script: a short Python script (no imports, no I/O) that calls tools as acme.<fn>(...) and returns a small result. Get signatures with search_tools. Use mode="dry_run" first for anything that writes.
Errors include an error_id; neurouter_explain_error(error_id) tells you how to fix the call. Search "neurouter" to find the other helper tools.

ro_tools_list.title: Run a Python script against the API
ro_tools_list.description: Run a short Python script that calls API tools as functions (e.g. acme.list_orders()) and returns a JSON-serializable value with `return`. No imports, no files, no network: only the tool functions, built-ins (len, sorted, isinstance, type, iter/next, …; no map/filter/getattr) and ops.* helpers. Tool results are whole dicts/lists inside scripts (no maxItems/maxBytes cuts); the script result limit applies to what you return. Use mode="dry_run" to see planned writes without executing them. Get function signatures from search_tools.
